acually look rectangular,
maybe to accomodate for the external frame, which

The ompartment separaor floor also has the curved

This bottom compartment zipper is inserted into the
seam between the superior and ingerior section. The
ends of the sipper do somethng tricky and the exct
mechanics of sewing it this way look very
inconvenient for whoever sewed this. There are
definitely some relief cuts in the seam allowance.
Reminds me a lot of the termination of the sippers
in Kånken backpack.

text.tspan: - some similar detail, e.g same buckles, but otherwise definitely different.
- the 905 is the only external frame ruck in the 1979 catalog
- tot me this 1979 model already looks more developed than our rucksack (a later model)

tspan.tspan: In the 1980 catalog, we get the same savotta logo on the cover as
is embroidered on the patch sewn onto the pack
This frame for the 905 and 807 has many similarities to the frame
we're trying to identify.
- same metal tri-gile for the load lifter to attach to the frame
- same shape and material for the shulder harness' padded
shoulder strap
- same adjustment buckle of the load lifter tensioner
But,
- top of the frame is different
- the O-ring that we have at the end of the shoulder harness
padding is sewn into the actual inferior section of the shoulder
strap. The O-ring is present, but sewn in slightly differently
- out shoulder stap padding, though t§he same, is not sewn into
the back support panel the way it is in this version.
Compared ot 810, our pack has a different frame, but the same
brown/beige mesh-webbing based support panels for the hip and
shoulder blades
This has the same shoulder strap padding and rigging, but
different rucksack, back support panels, and frame.
this has the same back support panels and very similar closusre
mechanism on the rain cover. Also the same amount of exterior
pockets. However, we're seemingly missing the zipper access to
the bottom compartment, and the shoulder harness and frame are
different.
1980, catalog v2
- Here we get No. 656, this notably has an orange external frame.
The deign of the frame is not the same, though. This lacks the
frame loop at the top bar of the frame, and it also has a bottom
shelf, which we don't have in out frame.
- Our frame also has a sticker that says "DURALUMIN", but the
catalog says this frame is steel, not duraluminum. Of course, the
sticer might have just been slapped onto our frame after the
fact.

text.tspan: - similar rain cover closure straps that terminate close to the shoulder harness bottom anchor point
- similar single cross-bag compression strap going from seam-to-seam across the posterior panel
- similar zipper grab handle on the bottom compartment zipper termination
- same shape and amount of exterior pockets.
All in all, this design is very similar. But it's obviously a different vesion.

tspan.tspan: 1971 cover image
The bag in this cover image very close to our bag.
- same design in the frame, with the metal loops for the vertical compression straps
- same side pockets
- same bottom compartment
- same bottom compartment zipper pull tab
- same cross-bag horizontal compression strap
- same plastic edge binding along the raincover and side pocket flaps
Only differences I can see are
- fabric color
- plastic buckles instead of metal ones
- the vertical compression straps going from frame-to-frame. In ours they are sewn into
the bottom edge of the raincover.
But that's really the only somewhat major difference. Changing fabric color and buckle
types is only a manufacturig step. And the vertical compression strap is not a big
change. Ours is made the ways it was in N:o 132 in 1971
